newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Friday were seen trading steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by adequate numbers of hogs and light packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Packer buying Friday was seen light amid ongoing slaughter reductions due to unprofitable operating margins, they said.
USDA estimated week-to-date slaughter at 1,274,000 head, under 1,306,000 in the same period last week.
Moderate hog movement on Thursday reportedly was enough to meet light packer demand, with several packer buyers saying they had the hogs needed for Friday's slaughter.
Weekend slaughter also was seen small, which was expected to further reduce packer buying on Friday, sources said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen at $58.50 to $59.00 and Illinois top prices at the plant could range $59.00 to $59.50.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant were seen $59.00 to $59.50, dealers and packer buyers there said.

Slaughter on Thursday was estimated at 331,000 head, compared with 330,000 a week ago and 320,000 a year ago, USDA reported. The week-to-date kill of 1.274 million head was down 2.5 percent compared with the same period a week ago at 1.306 million, USDA statistics showed.
